cards.explanation: The answer is abandon it. Verse 2 says it plainly: "do not abandon my directive." The father calls his teaching sound, and then he asks his sons to stick with it. Walking away from good teaching is like leaving a perfect dough out on the counter all night. Stay with it, friends.

The answer is True. Verse 3 says the father was once a son to his own father. Then verse 4 says, "…he taught me and said…" and the words that follow are what the father is now passing along. So the teaching is coming down from his own dad. That's three generations in one little passage, friends.

The answer is forget them or turn from them. Verse 5 says, "do not forget my words or turn from them." Grandpa wants his son to remember the words and to keep facing them. Forgetting and turning away are the two ways to lose them. Keep them close, friends.

The answer is guard. Verse 6 says, "love her, and she will guard you." Grandpa talks about wisdom like a person who looks out for whoever loves her. That's a pretty good bodyguard to have, friends. And she doesn't charge by the hour.

The answer is True. Verse 7 says, "Wisdom is supreme; so acquire wisdom. And whatever you may acquire, gain understanding." Grandpa calls wisdom supreme, and then he says to gain understanding whatever else you acquire. A full cookie jar is nice, but this is the part worth getting.

The answer is a garland of grace. Verse 9 says, "She will set a garland of grace on your head…" A garland is a wreath for the head, and this one is made of grace. Then comes a crown of beauty too. I think I'd wear that over my chef's hat, friends, and I'd make it work.

The answer is many years of life. Verse 10 says, "Listen, my son, and receive my words, and the years of your life will be many." The father ties his words to a long life. Listening counts for a lot here. It's just ears and a willing heart, friends.

The answer is False, because the father says the opposite. Verse 12 reads, "When you walk, your steps will not be impeded; when you run, you will not stumble." So the paths of wisdom are clear for walking and for running. Running, he says, comes with no stumbling.
The answer is life. Verse 13 says, "Guard it, for it is your life." The father isn't calling instruction a nice extra. He's calling it your life. That's worth guarding, friends.

The answer is False. He doesn't allow it at all. Verse 14 says, "Do not set foot on the path of the wicked…" and verse 15 adds, "Avoid it; do not travel on it. Turn from it and pass on by." Not a toe on that road, friends. Just keep walking past it.

The answer is make someone fall. Verse 16 says, "they are deprived of slumber until they make someone fall." That one is heavy, because it's about making someone fall. The father is showing his son what the wicked path is like. I think that's why he says to stay far away from it.

The answer is that it shines brighter until midday. Verse 18 says the path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, "…shining brighter and brighter until midday." So the light keeps growing. The father compares the path to dawn, from its first gleam on toward midday. I like that picture, friends.

The answer is False, because they don't know. Verse 19 says, "But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble." The father compares their way to the darkest gloom. What makes them stumble is something they do not know. That's a hard picture, friends.
The answer is heart. Verse 21 says, "keep them within your heart." The father wants his words down deep, not just in your ears. Then they go where you go. A heart makes a good pocket, friends.

The answer is True, friends. The father says his words are "…life to those who find them, and health to the whole body." (Proverbs 4:22). He's not talking about a quick pep talk here. He says these sayings reach the whole body, and that's a big claim for a few lines from a dad. I've had mixers that promised less and delivered way less.

The answer is that springs of life flow from it. Verse 23 says, "Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow springs of life." The reason is right there in the verse: springs of life flow from the heart. I think of a spring as the place where the water starts, so that's the spot you'd keep watch over. Guard the source, friends.
The answer is forward. Verse 25 says, "Let your eyes look forward; fix your gaze straight ahead." The father wants the gaze fixed on what's ahead. Eyes forward, friends.

The answer is don't swerve right or left. Verse 27 says, "Do not swerve to the right or to the left; turn your feet away from evil." Stay on the level path and keep going straight. No drifting to either side, friends.
